reason: Confirmed by driving, and worse than the finding states. undoBar() is emitted between .b-two and foot() in ownerSurface (render-b.js ~574), so the one .b-undo sits at the foot of the whole field. Opened at state=owner-editing and pressing 'Move a week later' once, the bar paints data-empty="false" but its viewport top measures 2263 in 390x844, 2310 in 768x1024, and 1911 in 1280x800, 1280x900 and 1440x960 — inViewport false at every width, at scrollY 0, at the exact moment the live region has something to say. The pointer claim also holds: below 1280 .b-edit is position:fixed (b.css .b-edit, static only inside the >=1280 .b-editHost rule), and scrolled fully to the bottom the bar's centre returns elementFromPoint inside .b-edit — a plain DIV of the panel at 390, .b-stepRead at 768 — so with the editor open the Undo control is unreachable by pointer at any scroll position at both sheet widths. At >=1280 it is reachable, but only after scrolling ~1200px away from the change. None of the gate's undo assertions (exists, count===1, role=status, names a key, silent at rest, control restores the item) touch position or reachability, so this is not a restatement. The mechanism proposed is also sound where it is tested: appendChild moves rather than clones, so count stays 1, role="status" and the Ctrl Z kbd ride along, the .b-undoAct click listener bound once in wireOwner survives the move, and paintUndo's root.querySelector needs no change. The re-render hazard named in the brief is not real: mount() clears host.textContent and rebuilds the whole tree including a fresh undoBar(), and the resize listener only calls settle(), never mount() — so a re-render discards and rebuilds both nodes rather than losing one. But the fix as written fails at the three desktop widths, and the assertion it proposes would fail with it. Simulated in the page — move the real .b-undo to be the last child of .b-edit, then press +7 — it lands inViewport true and reachable true at 390x844 (bar 712-815) and 768x1024 (945-995), but the rail editor already runs 546-1049 at desktop, so the appended bar measures 929-1032: inViewport false and elementFromPoint null at 1280x800, 1280x900 and 1440x960. Appending puts it below the fold of the very panel it is meant to be beside.
sharpenedFix: Same one-node move, but insert it at the TOP of the panel, not the foot, and sequence the move-back before the removal. In openEditor(), after the editor node is in the DOM: var u = root.querySelector('.b-undo'); if (u) node.insertBefore(u, node.firstChild). Simulated at all five viewports that lands the bar at 366-469 (390x844), 622-672 (768x1024) and 583-686 (1280x800, 1280x900, 1440x960) — inViewport true, elementFromPoint inside .b-undo, count 1, role=status at every one. Appending as last child does not; do not append. In closeEditor(), move it back BEFORE .b-edit is removed, and move it back even on the early return path: hoist the move above 'var node = root.querySelector(".b-edit"); if (node) node.remove();' and above 'if (!open) return;', re-inserting with root.insertBefore(u, root.querySelector('.b-foot')). If the move-back runs after node.remove(), the single bar is destroyed with the panel, paintUndo's querySelector returns null and returns early, and the reversibility surface is dead for the rest of the mount — the gate would not catch it, because it only counts .b-undo with the editor open. The same applies to the data-act="delete" path, which calls closeEditor(root,false) before item.remove(); routing every close through the fixed closeEditor covers it. CSS: since it now reads as the panel's head, use margin:0 0 4px and border-bottom:1px solid var(--fore-16) on .b-edit .b-undo (not margin-top/border-top), keeping its normal 20px top margin when it is back in the field. Then add the missing assertions, and add them at every viewport in elevate.config.json, not only 1440x960: after one stepper press with the editor open, assert the bar's rect is fully inside the viewport, that document.elementFromPoint at its centre resolves inside .b-undo, and — the case the round-1 wording lets through — assert after closeEditor that document.querySelectorAll('.b-undo').length is still 1 and paintUndo still finds it.
